 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA  ORAL ORDER 5 12-12-2024 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. Present prayer of bail along with suspension of sentence under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the "Cr.P.C.")/Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short the "B.N.S.S.") which has been raised through memo of appeal itself as preferred under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C./Section 415(2) of the B.N.S.S. against the judgment of conviction dated 21.08.2023 and order of sentence dated Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4984 of 2023(5) dt.12-12-2024 31.08.2023 passed by learned 6th Additional Sessions Judge- cum-Special Judge, POCSO(I), Muzaffarpur in connection with G.R. No. 53/2021 arising out of Railway P.S. Case No. 29 of 2021 whereby appellant has been convicted for the offence under section 366 of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years and a fine of Rs. 5,000/-, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo S.I. for three months and further convicted for the offence under Section 376 and Section 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten (10) years and fine of Rs. 20,000/-, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo S.I. for one year, thereafter, learned trial court ordered that all the sentences shall run concurrently.

3. It is submitted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/convict that the victim, as Sudhir Mallik @ Sujit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189034681/
1 per her radiological examination, was found between the age group of 16 - 17 years as per the testimony of PW-6 and PW-7.

sentences.text:
5. It is further submitted that the victim, as per her own statement, accompanied with the appellant/convict as per her own sweet-will and solemnized her marriage with appellant, thereafter,
she remained with him for one and half month.

It is pointed out by learned counsel that as certain differences took place between appellant and the victim after the marriage as she came to know that appellant also solemnized his marriage prior to this marriage, she took U- Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.4984 of 2023(5) dt.12-12-2024 turn while testifying before the court as PW-1 by giving occurrence as her kidnapping.
6. It is further submitted that PW-6 is the doctor, who conducted medical examination upon the victim, did not find anything which may corroborate with allegation of penetrative sexual assault/rape.
It is pointed out that with aforesaid evidence, it cannot be said that victim was a sterling witness so as on her sole testimony conviction can be recorded by the learned trial court.

7. While concluding argument, it is submitted that with aforesaid evidence, appellant/convict remains in custody for three and half years against fixed term sentence of ten (10) years, where this appeal is of November 2023 itself and same is not likely to be heard finally in near future, and as such, on this ground alone, appellant/convict deserves bail.
8.

Learned A.P.P. for the State, while opposing the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence of the appellant/convict, pointed out the testimony of the victim where she stated during her cross-examination that she did not accompanied appellant/convict out of her own sweet-will Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4984 of 2023(5) dt.12-12-2024 and, therefore, conviction as recorded by the learned trial court under Section 366 I.P.C.
appears justified.

It is submitted that cursory examination of testimony is not permissible at this stage, however, he could not disputed the factual submissions of learned counsel appearing for the appellant, as stated above, including custody period.

9. In view of aforesaid factual submissions and by taking note of statement of victim, as recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and also her testimony as PW-1 in totality, readwith testimony of PW-6 and PW-7 who examined victim medically, coupled with the fact that appellant remains in custody Sudhir Mallik @ Sujit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189034681/
2 for about three and half years against fixed term sentence of ten (10) years, where this appeal is of November 2023 itself and same is not likely to be heard finally in near future, accordingly,
appellant/convict above-named is directed to be released on bail, during pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 6th Additional Sessions Judge-cum- Special Judge,
POCSO(I), Muzaffarpur in connection with Patna High Court CR.
